paccayasutta:
[Paccaya+sutta]  CL=8 The Paccaya Sutta (SN12.27): This is a discourse where the Buddha explains in detail the relationship between causes (Paticca-samuppada) and effects (Paticca-samuppanna). The sutta explains that aging (jara) and death (marana) arise due to birth (jati). When birth ceases, aging and death also cease. The Noble Eightfold Path is the right practice that leads to Nibbana, where aging (jara) and death (marana) are completely extinguished.
This sutta is significant because it:
1. Demonstrates the causal relationship in dependent origination
2. Shows how birth leads to aging and death
3. Explains that the Noble Eightfold Path is the way to end this cycle
4. Points to Nibbana as the state where aging and death are completely extinguished

yathābhūtapaṭivedhana: [Yathābhūta+paṭivedhana] (na) CL=7 Insight which is seen clearly as the matter of fact and   is not change (for the worse)/is not formation.
yathāpariccheda: [Yathā+pariccheda] (ti) CL=7 (1) Should be demarcated (period). (Na) (2) As per division. (3) The division which you have made. See original.
yathāpavattamāna: [Yathā+pavattamāna] (ti) CL=7 As it is being as usual.
yathāvuttarūpa: [Yathāvutta+rūpa] (ti) CL=7 (1) It has  the nature which have said/mentioned. (Na) (2) Physical form which has different kinds.
yāthāvadassana: [Yāthāva+dassana] (na) CL=7 It can be seen as the matter of fact ( physical form and consciousness).
yiṭṭhukāma: [Yaja+tuṃ=yiṭṭhuṃ+kamu+ṇa] (ti) CL=7 One who desires to offer a sacrifice, One who want to offer a sacrifice.
yogagocchaka: [Yoga+gocchaka] (pu) CL=7 All of sum Dutas which is related mually by meaning of sadda such as Yogaduka, All of sum Dutas which like bunch of flowers such as Yogaduka.
yojanagaṇana: [Yojana+gaṇana] (na) CL=7 Many Yojana, a lot of Yojana, a hundred Yojana, a thousand Yūjanā.(Yojana means measure of distance equal to 12.72 miles).
yuva: [Yu+a] (pu) CL=7 Yu-missane, a, uvādeso, sissākāro. Dhāna, ṭī. 253. Yuvana-saṃ. Yuva-prā.] (1) One who is fresh and youthful, Child. (2) (A) A young man, Bachelor. (B) One who is the first stage of life span, One who comes of age and have strength. (The first stage of life span means the age from 16 years and 20 years). See original.
yuñjanabhāva: [Yuñjana+bhāva] (pu) CL=7 As the state of making effort.
yūthikapupphiya: [Yūthikapupphi+iya] (ti) CL=7 One who is offering Jasmine flowers, Jvana flowers (small fragrant white flower Jasminum auriculatum).
